e: The Sandiganbayan acquits former Albay governor Edcel Greco Lagman of indirect bribery and violations of the anti-jueteng law, citing insufficient evidence.
The Sandiganbayan orders a 90-day preventive suspension of Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez in relation to charges of plunder.
The effectivity of a previous year's proclamation declaring a state of national calamity for a year due to the effects of Typhoon Kalmaegi (Tino) ends.
The Supreme Court publicizes its February 4 ruling emphasizing that men can also be victims of sexual violence, in a 2018 case where a woman was later convicted.
PHIVOLCS raises anew Alert Level 3 over Mayon volcano in Albay following a six-minute moderately explosive eruption.
Abdulraof Macacua, the incumbent interim chief minister of Bangsamoro, becomes the first to be elected for the same position by the first regular regional parliament during their inaugural session.

President Marcos issues Executive Order No. 130 allowing the independent suspension of in-person classes in schools based on any threats, and resumption of such while disregarding any existing suspension order from the local government.
Two SF-260 trainer aircraft of the Philippine Air Force crash after colliding with each other mid-air over Fernando Air Base in Lipa, Batangas, killing four pilots.

The Supreme Court, acting on four separate petitions, declares unconstitutional the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts and certain provisions in the 2026 GAA, citing adjustments made by the Congress involving the unprogrammed and special funds. However, the SC declares the application of the doctrine of operative fact (recognition of the validity of a law prior to the decision) in its decision on the first two GAAs.
The Sandiganbayan orders a 90-day suspension of Senator Rodante Marcoleta due to his plunder case.
A state of calamity is declared in Iloilo due to the RSSI infestation on sugarcane fields. Similar declarations are made earlier in Dueñas, Passi and San Enrique.

The Philippine Competition Commission imposes a fine of P1.76 billion pesos ($27.9 million) on six companies for forming a cartel that artificially raised the price of onions in 2022, making it the largest penalty imposed by the agency since its establishment in 2016.
The Sandiganbayan acquits former health secretary Janette Garin of graft involving P3 billion used in the procurement of Dengvaxia vaccines and the school-based immunization program.
The Sandiganbayan orders another 90-day preventive suspension of Senator Jinggoy Estrada in relation to charges of graft.

A state of calamity is declared in Lope de Vega, Northern Samar, due to the impact of prolonged drought. The municipality is the Eastern Visayas' first to be placed under such due to El Niño; and is later followed by Gandara, Samar.

A state of calamity is declared in Dueñas, Iloilo, due to agricultural damages caused by the RSSI infestation and a dry spell. The municipality is the Western Visayas' first to be placed under such due to El Niño; and is later followed by Lambunao.

In Luang Prabang, Laos, a drug smuggling scheme is thwarted by Laotian police at Luang Prabang International Airport involving a private jet from Malaysia planning to transport methamphetamine to the Philippines. This leads to a joint investigation by authorities in Malaysia and the Philippines after a Filipino politician is suspected to have been involved.
Manibela and Piston hold a nationwide transportation strike in protest against rising fuel prices.
President Marcos issues Executive Order No. 125, suspending anew excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene.

President Marcos grants absolute pardon to Mary Jane Veloso, who had been imprisoned since 2010 for heroin smuggling in Indonesia, was reprieved from execution in 2015 and sent back to the country in 2024. She is released from the Correctional Institution for Women in Mandaluyong the following day.
The Department of Information and Communications Technology imposes a ban on Discord in the country, citing security reasons. The ban is subsequently lifted amid heavy criticism from users.

The Sandiganbayan imposes a 90-day preventive suspension on Uswag Ilonggo party-list representative Jojo Ang after he is charged with graft over alleged conflict of interest in infrastructure projects.
Three students are killed ‌while eight others are injured in a mass shooting at a secondary school in Banga, South Cotabato.
The Ombudsman orders the dismissal of Duero, Bohol mayor Al Taculad, citing conflict of interest in the awarding of P79.33 million in government infrastructure projects in the municipality in 2023.
The BFAR vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat is damaged after being struck by a China Coast Guard vessel in the South China Sea off the coast of Palawan.

A state of calamity is declared in Camarines Norte due to the water shortage. The province is the Bicol Region's first to be placed under such due to El Niño. Similar declarations are made earlier in the municipalities of San Lorenzo Ruiz and San Vicente.
The Supreme Court rules that Congress has a mandatory duty to pass a law to ban political dynasties in the country under the Constitution following a consolidated petition submitted by civic groups.
Manibela holds a nationwide transportation strike in protest against rising fuel prices.

The Supreme Court publicizes its decision dated June 10 acquitting former first lady Imelda Marcos by overturning her 2018 conviction by the Sandiganbayan of seven of ten counts of graft which were filed in 1991 in relation to Swiss foundations.
The passenger vessel MV June Aster sailing from Manila catches fire before reaching Coron, Palawan, killing at least 77 people and leaving eight others missing.

Former House speaker Martin Romualdez is arrested while seeking medical treatment at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan, Metro Manila on charges of plunder relating to the flood control scandal.
President Marcos signs into law Republic Act No. 12325, amending the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act and increasing government assistance to tertiary education students.

A court in Quezon City issues an arrest warrant against vice president Duterte on charges of grave threats regarding statements she made in 2024 against President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Duterte posts bail the following day.

A special election for a member of the House of Representatives in the 4th district of Cavite is held. Incumbent Dasmariñas mayor Jenny Barzaga, mother of expelled representative Kiko, is elected replacing the latter, and is sworn into office on September 1.

A state of calamity is declared in Guinayangan, Quezon, due to drought and the resulting water shortage. The municipality is the Calabarzon's first to be placed under such due to El Niño, and is later followed by Alabat, General Nakar, Jomalig and Lopez.
The Urology Center of the Philippines, Inc. in Quezon City conducts the country's first remote surgery from Shanghai, China.
Japan–Philippines relations: The Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement between the Philippines and Japan, whose main agreement was signed in January, enters into force.
Bimmy Alonto, the vice mayor of Marantao, Lanao del Sur, is arrested in Iligan on charges of murder and frustrated murder.
Two students, including the gunman, are killed while more than 20 others are injured in a mass shooting at the Ateneo de Zamboanga Junior High School in Zamboanga City.

President Marcos signs Executive Order (EO) No. 123 which reverts the administrative supervision over the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor and the National Anti-Poverty Commission from the Department of Social Welfare and Development to the Office of the President, partially reversing EO No. 67 of 2018.
